import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The operator UI is themed by one set of CSS custom properties. The **default
theme is "bluefrost"** (id `frost`, label "Blue frost" — deep sky-tinted dark
surfaces, frost-white text, a sky accent), generated from DTCG token JSON;
built-in **"black"** and **"honeycomb"** themes (plus a legacy **"pot"** alias,
superseded by honeycomb and kept only for old previews) plus **user-created
custom themes** swap the same variables (see [Themes](#themes--frost--black--custom)).
This page is the reference for what exists, **the contract agents must follow**,
and how to change it.

<Aside type="caution" title="Not the same system as design-phase:list_tokens (EI-604)">
`design-phase:list_tokens` reads a stale, disconnected light-mode `react-tailwind`
palette — it does **not** reflect the tokens on this page. This page (the
`design-tokens/*.tokens.json` → `_semantic.css` pipeline below) is the operator's
real, live token system. Use this page for any operator UI token work.
</Aside>

<Aside type="danger" title="The one rule: never hardcode a brand color">
Components must reference a **semantic `var(--…)` token**, never a brand
primitive (`--sky-400`, `--sky-300`, …) and never a raw sky literal (`#38bdf8`,
`#7dd3fc`, `#bae6fd`, `rgba(125, 211, 252, …)`, …). A theme can only swap the
**semantic** layer — anything hardcoded to a sky value stays blue when the user
picks Black. This rule is partly test-enforced and partly review-enforced:
`app/_lints/css-tokens.test.ts` checks that every `var(--…)` reference in
`.tsx` resolves to a defined token, and `app/_lints/design-primitives.test.ts`
blocks brand primitive references plus direct cyan literals in audited active
surfaces. The audit is intentionally not whole-repo yet, so the full do/don't is
still binding review policy; see the
[theme contract](#the-theme-contract--what-agents-must-follow) below.
</Aside>

<Aside type="caution" title="Never hand-edit the generated CSS">
`apps/operator/app/_brand-primitives.css` and `apps/operator/app/_semantic.css`
both start with `/** Do not edit directly, this file was auto-generated. */`.
Edit the token JSON and re-run the build — a hand edit is overwritten on the
next `npm run tokens`.
</Aside>

## The pipeline

```
design-tokens/*.tokens.json        ← source of truth (DTCG)
        │  npm run tokens  (Style Dictionary v4 — design-tokens/style-dictionary.config.mjs)
        ▼
apps/operator/app/_brand-primitives.css   ← primitives tier  (--sky-400, --emerald-400, …)
apps/operator/app/_semantic.css           ← semantic tier    (--bg, --fg, --accent, …)
        │  imported at the top of
        ▼
apps/operator/app/globals.css      → every operator + /adv surface
```

Source files under `design-tokens/`:

| File | Tier | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `primitives.tokens.json` | primitive | Raw brand palette — `sky` / `emerald` / `amber` / `gold` / `rose` / `slate`. Canonical for **all** platforms (mobile mirrors it). |
| `desktop.semantic.tokens.json` | semantic | Desktop `--bg` / `--fg` / `--accent` / `--warn` etc., aliased to primitives. The default (frost) layer. |
| `black.semantic.tokens.json`, `pot.semantic.tokens.json`, `honeycomb.semantic.tokens.json` | semantic | Theme override sets (one namespace each — `black.*`, `pot.*`, `honeycomb.*`), emitted under `[data-theme="<name>"]`. `black` + `honeycomb` are the selectable built-ins; `pot` is a legacy alias (superseded by honeycomb). |
| `desktop.motion.tokens.json` | semantic | `--ease-*` / `--dur-*` easing + duration tokens. |
| `style-dictionary.config.mjs` | build | SD v4 config that emits the brand + semantic CSS files (frost base + one per theme). |

Regenerate after editing any token JSON (the dev server does **not** auto-run it):

```bash
npm run tokens     # re-emit _brand-primitives.css + _semantic.css (+ the per-theme files)
```

If you change a **primitive** (a brand color), also re-mirror mobile
(`make tokens` in `papercup-rust-mobile/`). Changing only a desktop **semantic**
needs no mobile touch. Full guide: `design-tokens/README.md`.

## The bluefrost semantic scale

These are the variables new UI should use — never a raw hex. Each has a fallback
baked in (`var(--bg, #07101d)`) so a component renders correctly even outside the
themed tree.

| Token | Value | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `--bg-deepest` `--bg-deeper` `--bg-deep` | `#02060c` / `#030a14` / `#050d18` | **Surface depth scale** — below the page: deepest gradient stops / deep surfaces / sub-base. Use these for dark gradients & shadows instead of a hand-picked navy literal. |
| `--bg` | `#07101d` | Page / app background. |
| `--bg-1` | `#0b1220` | Panel background — one step up from the page. |
| `--bg-2` `--bg-3` `--bg-4` | translucent white 4.5% / 7.5% / 12% | Surface tiers: inputs, chips, hover, raised. |
| `--bg-popover` | `#0d1829` | Solid elevated surface for menus / hover cards / popovers. |
| `--bg-raised` `--bg-raised-high` | `#112235` / `#143049` | Solid raised panel above the page/popover band; `-high` is the lighter emphasis/hover variant. Use instead of the bespoke panel-navy literal. |
| `--fg` | `#e7f7ff` | Primary text. |
| `--fg-dim` | `#b9d4e8` | Secondary text. |
| `--fg-mute` | `#7f9bb4` | Tertiary / metadata text. |
| `--border-muted` | sky-300 @ 0.08 | Faintest border step — one below `--border`, e.g. table row dividers. |
| `--border` `--border-strong` | sky-300 @ 0.15 / 0.32 | Hairline / emphasized borders (sky-tinted, the bluefrost signature). |
| `--accent` `--accent-strong` `--accent-cool` | sky-400 / sky-300 / sky-cool | Interactive accent, hover, soft accent. |
| `--accent-soft` `--accent-deep` `--accent-deeper` | sky-200 / sky-500 / sky-700 | The **accent-tint scale** — lighter & deeper accent shades for glows, gradients, and HUD washes. Use these instead of the raw `sky-200/500/700` they alias. |
| `--accent-ink` | `#051827` | Text **on** an accent-filled background. |
| `--good` `--warn` `--bad` | emerald / amber / rose | Semantic status (success / warning / danger). |
| `--warn-bg` `--warn-border` | amber @ 0.1 / 0.35 | Warning banner fill + border. |
| `--ease-out` `--dur-fast` … | see `_semantic.css` | Motion — pair with `[data-anim]` per the [performance rules](/internal/docs/design/performance). |

**Tinting pattern.** Derive accent washes with `color-mix` over a token, never a
hardcoded rgba — it tracks the active theme automatically:

```css
background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent), transparent 86%); /* selected row */
border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent), transparent 55%);
```

**Migrating an existing `rgba(<sky>, a)` → use `in srgb`.** `color-mix(in srgb,
C, transparent N%)` resolves to *exactly* `C` at alpha `(1 − N/100)` (premultiplied
mix with `transparent`), so it's **byte-identical** to the old rgba in frost and
goes monochrome in black. Pick the token whose frost value equals the sky shade:

| Old literal | Replace with |
|---|---|
| `var(--sky-300)`, `#7dd3fc`, `rgba(125,211,252,a)` | `--accent-strong` / `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent-strong), transparent {(1−a)·100}%)` |
| `var(--sky-400)`, `#38bdf8`, `rgba(56,189,248,a)` | `--accent` / `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent), …)` |
| `#d7f3ff`, `rgba(215,243,255,a)` | `--accent-cool` |
| `#bae6fd`, `rgba(186,230,253,a)` | `--accent-soft` |
| `#0ea5e9`, `rgba(14,165,233,a)` | `--accent-deep` |
| `#0369a1`, `rgba(3,105,161,a)` | `--accent-deeper` |
| `#67e8f9` (cyan-300), `rgba(103,232,249,a)` | `--accent-strong` / `rgb(from var(--accent-strong) r g b / a)` (nearest sky shade; also `--accent-strong-rgb` for `rgba(var(--accent-strong-rgb), a)` triplet composition) |
| `#22d3ee` (cyan-400), `rgba(34,211,238,a)` | `--accent` / `rgb(from var(--accent) r g b / a)` (nearest sky shade; `--accent-rgb` for triplet composition) |

(`in oklab` is fine for *new* washes; use `in srgb` when you're replacing an
existing rgba and need the frost render to stay pixel-for-pixel identical.)

## The theme contract — what agents must follow

A theme (frost, black, a custom one) is a swap of the **semantic** layer only.
For that swap to actually re-skin the UI, components must route every color
through it. The rules:

1. **Never write a brand primitive in a component.** No `var(--sky-400)`,
   `var(--sky-300)`, … in any `.tsx`/`.css`. Those are the raw palette; they
   don't move when the theme changes.
2. **Never write a sky/cyan literal.** No `#38bdf8` / `#7dd3fc` / `#bae6fd` /
   `#d7f3ff` / `#0ea5e9` hexes and no `rgba(125,211,252,…)` / `rgba(56,189,248,…)`
   etc. Use the semantic token (or a `color-mix` over one — see the migration
   table above).
3. **A `var(--token, #fallback)` fallback is fine and encouraged** — the token
   wins; the literal only applies if the var is somehow undefined. That's *not*
   a leak. (`border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(125,211,252,0.15))` ✓.)
4. **Surfaces use the `--bg` family**, text the `--fg` family, borders
   `--border`/`--border-strong`, accents the `--accent` family (incl. the
   accent-tint scale). New dark surfaces → `--bg` / `--bg-1` / `--bg-popover`,
   **never** a hand-picked dark-navy literal.
5. **Status & decorative palettes are exempt** — see the next two sections.
6. **Brand marks, media, and swatches are narrow exceptions.** A logo SVG,
   avatar, screenshot, user-authored color swatch, or token-dev preview may
   carry its real color. If the color is part of app chrome, navigation,
   content panels, cards, buttons, or charts that should theme with the app, it
   must be semantic-tokenized.

<Aside type="tip" title="The litmus test">
Switch the operator to the **Black** theme (Settings → Personalization). Anything
still tinted blue is a leak — find the hardcoded sky value and route it through
the matching `--accent*` token. If swapping the semantic tokens *doesn't* restyle
your component, your component is the bug, not the theme system.
</Aside>

## Themes (frost / black / custom)

| Concern | How |
|---|---|
| Mechanism | `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` (`apps/operator/lib/theme.ts`). Frost is the `:root` default; `[data-theme="black"]` / `[data-theme="pot"]` / `[data-theme="honeycomb"]` / `[data-theme="custom:<id>"]` override the semantic vars. |
| Built-ins (frost, black, honeycomb) | `BUILTIN_THEMES` in `packages/operator-core/lib/theme-tokens.ts` (frost = "Blue frost", black, honeycomb). Authored in `design-tokens/*.semantic.tokens.json`, generated by Style Dictionary into `_semantic.css` (`:root` = frost), `_semantic.frost.css` (scopable frost), and one `_semantic.<name>.css` per theme (`[data-theme="<name>"]`). `pot` still generates a `[data-theme="pot"]` block but is a legacy alias, not in `BUILTIN_THEMES`. Add a built-in = a new token file + a `css-semantic-<name>` platform. ⚠ A theme that overrides `accent`/`accent-strong` **must also override `accent-rgb`/`accent-strong-rgb`** — the triplet tokens compose via `rgba(var(--accent-rgb), a)`, and a theme that omits them silently inherits frost's **sky** triplet through `:root` (the exact leak class the theme swap exists to prevent; found + fixed for black/honeycomb/pot 2026-07-09). |
| Custom themes | Persisted to a per-workspace local file (`papercuspPath('themes', 'custom.json')`, `packages/operator-core/lib/custom-themes.ts`); applied at runtime by injecting a `<style id="pc-custom-themes">` block (`apps/operator/lib/theme.ts`, `CUSTOM_THEMES_STYLE_ID`). Created in Settings → Personalization. |
| The allow-list | `THEME_TOKENS` in `packages/operator-core/lib/theme-tokens.ts` — the *only* tokens a theme may set; `validateCustomTheme` rejects anything else (also blocks CSS-injection). `design-tokens/tokens.test.ts` enforces the same contract for built-ins. |

Full design + history: the plan `personalization-theme-selector-2026-05-30`
(`apps/operator/docs/plans/`).

## Surfaces are tokenized too — use the depth scale, not a navy literal

Surfaces used to be the weak spot: ~1100 bespoke near-black navy literals
(`#07101d`, `rgb(6,13,24)`, `rgb(3,10,20)`, …) were hand-coded directly into
gradients and surfaces, *below* the `--bg` tokens — so they ignored the theme
switch and stayed navy under every theme. They were routed to the
**surface depth scale** (`--bg-deepest`/`--bg-deeper`/`--bg-deep` + `--bg`/`--bg-1`/
`--bg-popover`); each frost value matches the navy it replaced, so frost is
unchanged, while black and any custom theme fully recolor the surfaces.

**What this means for you:** for any dark surface, gradient stop, or shadow, reach
for a surface token (`--bg-deepest` … `--bg-popover`) or a `color-mix` over one —
**never** a hand-picked dark-navy literal. A raw navy is the exact debt that was
just paid down; re-introducing one re-breaks every theme but frost.

## Status colors — one canonical source

Per-status coloring (feature status, issue severity, issue status) is **not** a
per-component decision. It lives in three Proxy-guarded tables in
`apps/operator/app/harness/theme.ts` and is rendered through the pills in
`apps/operator/app/harness/primitives.tsx`:

| Table | Keys | Pill |
|---|---|---|
| `STATUS` | `todo` · `in_progress` · `validating` · `failing` · `blocked` · `passed` · `deprecated` | `<StatusPill status={…} />` |
| `SEVERITY` | `critical` · `major` · `minor` · `nit` | `<SeverityPill severity={…} />` |
| `ISSUE_STATUS` | `open` · `acknowledged` · `fixing` · `resolved` · `closed` · `wontfix` | `<IssueStatusPill status={…} />` |

Each entry is `{ solid, bg, text, label }`. The hues are semantic (red →
amber → sky → grey for severity, etc.) and chosen to read on the bluefrost dark
surfaces — `SEVERITY.minor` uses the sky accent rather than a legacy yellow to
stay on-theme. The same tables back the legacy `/harness` route, so `/adv` and
`/harness` show identical status coloring.

The three tables above are scoped to *status* coloring, but the same
`harness/theme.ts` holds the broader single-source family: the Proxy-guarded
**`kind`** tables `WORK_ITEM_KIND` (rendered by `<KindPill>`) and `AGENT_KIND`
(rendered by `<AgentKindPill>`) follow the identical pattern — so work-item kind
and agent kind coloring is likewise **not** a per-component decision.

<Aside type="tip" title="Do / don't">
**Do** reach for a `var(--…)` semantic token and the `STATUS`/`SEVERITY`/`ISSUE_STATUS`
pills. **Don't** declare a local `STATUS_TONE` / `SEVERITY_TONE` map or a raw hex
in a component — that's the exact drift this single source exists to prevent
(three divergent copies had crept into the `/adv` Harness panels before the
2026-05-30 redesign consolidated them).
</Aside>
